long_biography.plain_text:
Jimmy John's founder Jimmy John Liautaud originally wanted to sell hot dogs, but the equipment cost pushed him towards sandwiches. Used equipment and a small menu made the alternative affordable. Working alone after his initial helpers left, he learned every part of running the shop, from serving customers to tracking the cash used to pay suppliers.

Expansion revealed a different challenge: franchisees did not automatically share his appetite for the daily work. Liautaud paused new franchise sales and travelled with company president James North to retrain struggling operators. They tightened the standards for admitting new franchisees and made the long hours and practical demands explicit. Regular training became central to reproducing the service that had worked in his own restaurants.
